- When sentiment shows strong positive bias (e.g., >0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment shows strong negative bias (e.g., <0.33) or sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust downward with lagged momentum or add volatility buffer.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >85), model frequently overcorrects or overshoots; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or apply mean reversion to 30d moving average.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 14d or 30d moving average as anchor for correction.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns sharply negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- When sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (e.g., alternating 0.67 and 0.33), model tends to overfit trend; apply smoothing or dampen trend component by 20–30%.
